newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey assesses bids in barley export tender.
newsitem.headline: Turkey assesses bids in barley export tender.

text.p: Turkey's state grain board (TMO) on Thursday began assessing bids from eight international and local firms for its barley export tender, officials said.
They said the result of the tender, announced earlier to be at least for 200,000 tonnes of feed and malting barley, could be made public later in the day or on early Friday.
Participating companies were Tradigrain, Romak, Louis Dreyfus, Alfred Toepfer International, Glencore, Cargill International, Grains and Fourrages, and the local firm BEM.

The fob prices for feed barley ranged from $121 per tonne, given by Tradigrain for 50,000 tonnes with November and December shipment, to $136.07, by Glencore for 125,000 tonnes with shipments in the second half of October.
Feed barley shipment dates varied from October to end-December.

Fob prices for malting barley were in the range from $148 per tonne to $150.75. Only Alfred Toepfer and Glencore gave bids for malting barley for hauls of 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes with October and November shipments.
Shipments will be made mainly from Derince and Mersin ports but Iskenderun port was also included in some bids.
